messages.author: 2f9332f7ce03d2e6
messages.subject: DIF ParObjects Error
parts:
Hi Phil,

I've used the mirt package for running IRT (been great!), but having some trouble with the DIF analysis. 

My datafile has a Col1 as a Gender indicator, and the next columns are survey answers (0 or 1) for each student (row). I was getting the error:

> model <- multipleGroup(data, 1, data$Gender, invariance = '1')
> Error: Input data must be integer or numeric values only

So, I removed the Gender column and was able to get the mirt to work. I confirmed no missing data. Here 'dat' is just the student answer columns without the Gender column:

> mirt(dat, 1, itemtype = '2PL',SE=TRUE)
>Iteration: 28, Log-Lik: -3764.536, Max-Change: 0.00010

>Calculating information matrix...

>Call:
  mirt(data = dat, model = 1, itemtype = "2PL", SE = TRUE)

> Full-information item factor analysis with 1 factor(s).
  Converged within 1e-04 tolerance after 28 EM iterations.
   mirt version: 1.25 
  M-step optimizer: BFGS 
  EM acceleration: Ramsay 
  Number of rectangular quadrature: 61

  Information matrix estimated with method: Oakes
  Condition number of information matrix = 154.258
  Second-order test: model is a possible local maximum

  Log-likelihood = -3764.536
  Estimated parameters: 68 
  AIC = 7665.071; AICc = 7729.789
  BIC = 7893.958; SABIC = 7678.483


When I go to run the DIF with the gender (called 'Gender') data set (single column of M/F text gender) I'm getting the following error:


> DIF(mirt(dat, 1, itemtype = '2PL',SE=TRUE), Gender)
> Iteration: 28, Log-Lik: -3764.536, Max-Change: 0.00010
> Calculating information matrix...
> Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : 
   no slot of name "ParObjects" for this object of class "dich"

This is my first time running a DIF analysis so looking for some advice, thanks so much!

Jack

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DIF ParObjects Error
parts:
Well, this seems like a missed test on my part. The first object must be of class MultipleGroupClass, which is only obtainable through the multipleGroup() function in mirt. DIF() should have thrown an error message earlier. Try fitting the multiple group object first and giving  
DIF() another go. 
Phil

                DIF testing, freeing the focal group hyper-parameters is recommended.
Error: Item 1 does not contain any of the parameters defined in which.par.
                 Consider removing it from the item2test input or adding relevant parameters
                 to which.par



Best,

Jack
